answer_text:
Using all 8 digits \(0,1,1,1,4,4,4,6\), an 8-digit number is divisible by \(4\) iff its last two digits form a two-digit number divisible by \(4\).

Possible endings from these digits are:

\[
04,\;16,\;40,\;44,\;60,\;64
\]

Now count arrangements of the remaining 6 digits, making sure the first digit is not \(0\).

\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c}
\text{Ending} & \text{Remaining digits} & \text{Valid arrangements} \\
\hline
04 & 1,1,1,4,4,6 & \frac{6!}{3!2!}=60 \\
16 & 0,1,1,4,4,4 & \frac{6!}{2!3!}-\frac{5!}{2!3!}=60-10=50 \\
40 & 1,1,1,4,4,6 & \frac{6!}{3!2!}=60 \\
44 & 0,1,1,1,4,6 & \frac{6!}{3!}-\frac{5!}{3!}=120-20=100 \\
60 & 1,1,1,4,4,4 & \frac{6!}{3!3!}=20 \\
64 & 0,1,1,1,4,4 & \frac{6!}{3!2!}-\frac{5!}{3!2!}=60-10=50
\end{array}
\]

Adding:

\[
60+50+60+100+20+50=340
\]

\[
\boxed{340}
\]
